answer.rationale: Write-path p99 began climbing ~30 minutes after the release, making the new build the leading suspect; memory_b1 supports rollback as a fast, low-customer-impact recovery, while memory_b3 (pre-provisioned headroom) is less applicable since capacity was not provisioned ahead of this peak and adding capacity mid-peak may not address a regression-induced latency. Rolling back first is reversible and preserves writes; if latency persists post-rollback, failover or capacity can follow in the next window. Uncertainty remains because peak settlement load is a confounder, so I verify both candidate memories before committing.
